title: The Bright and the Better: A Lecture on Novelty and Effectiveness · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about a distinction that sounds simple but is surprisingly easy to miss: the difference between novelty and effectiveness. Novelty is about being new, different, or unusual. Effectiveness is about producing the result you actually want. A new idea can be exciting and still be ineffective. An old idea can be boring and still work very well. In this lecture, I will explain why we often confuse the two, and how to keep them separate when we make decisions. Let me start with a story from a simulated school project. A group of teachers wanted to improve reading scores. One teacher suggested a brand-new app with games, badges, and daily challenges. The app was definitely novel. Students had never seen anything like it. Another teacher suggested something much less exciting: twenty minutes of silent reading every morning, with a simple log sheet. No games. No badges. Just reading.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you prefer new methods or old methods? Why?
Can you describe a time when a new idea did not work well?
What do you think is more important: being new or being effective?
How do you decide if something is effective?

Part 2
Describe a situation where you had to choose between a new approach and an old approach. You should say: what the situation was; what the new approach was; what the old approach was; and explain which one you chose and why.

Part 3
Why do people often prefer new things?
How can we measure effectiveness in education?
Do you agree that old methods are always safer? Why or why not?
What role does evidence play in decision-making?
